Castle chronicle · selected January 2025 public scenes
body:
Caisleán na Brón is the adventurers’ Fein Uaill home made historical. Its January welcome records fields, vineyards and a home offered to the company. By August it serves as a private castle where people prepare to confront Aria’s political power; later it becomes a residence holding Aria’s possessions and old enemies beneath one roof, the place where a grieving Zarathian delegation arrives demanding answers, and finally a surviving refuge in a quieter order.

Name boundary: “Caselean de Broin,” “Caislean na Bron,” and “Caisleán De Bróin” remain searchable source forms. The newer chronicle also uses “Caisleán na Bróin.” The exact translation, naming date, builder, and legal deed are unresolved; the January welcome records the castle being given to the company.

5 August 2025 · political backstage

Before a public confrontation with Aria, adventurers gather in what the record calls “your castle.” The room functions as a place to compare risks, rehearse positions, and decide what can be said in public. The identification of this unnamed castle with later Caselean is a strong continuity inference rather than a directly preserved label.

19 August 2025 · newcomers wait and listen

Eldin Stormheart stays at the castle and listens while people discuss the tangled history of Magnus and Scribonia. Alongside its use as a command post, the castle gives a newer arrival somewhere to stay while others explain their old conflicts.

23 November 2025 · after Aria

The castle is explicitly called Caselean. Olokun has a room there, and Aria’s possessions are kept inside after her death. Eugene, Magnus, Arjahn, and others occupy the same domestic-political space while a Zarathian envoy and an immense body of troops approach. A residence becomes the threshold at which private grief meets national consequence.

Magnus and Arjahn stay under one roof despite their history. Arjahn carries profound grievance and does not pretend it has disappeared; he chooses not to turn the castle into another battlefield. Olokun keeps Aria’s belongings, leaving claims to inheritance and questions of forgiveness unsettled.

Court etiquette and political succession

Bowene’s delegation brings etiquette, succession, and the unresolved legitimacy of adventurer power to the castle door. Caselean is neither a sovereign capital nor a neutral zone in the recovered record. It is a political threshold: a private home important enough that history comes looking for its residents there.

29 July 2026 · respite

Later state-of-the-world testimony says people still dwell in Caselean de Broin and find respite there amid Fein Uaill’s abundance. The castle survives the immediate Aria crisis and becomes a home with accumulated layers rather than a set piece discarded after one confrontation.

Location timeline

  1. 5 Aug 2025

    An adventurer castle serves as private preparation space before public confrontation.

  2. 19 Aug 2025

    Eldin waits there while older histories are explained.

  3. 23 Nov 2025

    Caselean is named; Aria’s possessions, Magnus, Arjahn, Olokun, Eugene, and a Zarathian delegation converge.

  4. 29 Jul 2026

    The castle remains inhabited and is remembered as a place of respite.

Open record

The January welcome establishes the company’s acquisition of the residence and describes its fields, vineyards, courtyard and teleportation circle. The founding date, builder, legal title, complete layout, permanent residents and exact continuity of every unnamed castle scene remain incomplete. References to another “estate” must not be merged into this location without proof.

January 2025 · fields, vineyards and a new home

The earlier castle chronicle opens with the company arriving among wheat fields and grapevines. Tarwen of the Silver Star confirms that the castle is theirs, promises access to Zarathis through its teleportation circle, and leaves them privacy. Elenia thanks him for the splendid lodgings; Draygar wants to find the forge. The welcome names Elenia, Adelia, Draygar, Krone and Olokun as the company receiving the residence. It establishes a grant of use and possession, without preserving a legal deed, builder or founding date.

Hospitality without agreement

Luxury does not remove the company’s uncertainty. They worry about Eugene and Scribonia, disagree over local hostility toward the gods, and look for a way to communicate or travel beyond the region. Draygar says he will join the Silver Star; Olokun considers the Emerald Veil as a route to knowledge and cooperation with other islands. Their plans do not establish completed initiation for every resident.

A courtyard devoted to the light

Elenia makes a flower-filled meditation place around a stone in the courtyard, later calling it her altar to the light. She invokes Eugene with her glowing orb, and Adelia also asks for both missing friends to return. These early attempts produce no witnessed return. The altar’s purpose is companionship and recovery; the scene does not prove a resurrection, the safety of any proposed route, or the identity of the power answering her magic.

Eldin keeps renewing the wards

Eldin Stormheart walks the perimeter with a bagpipe-led ritual and casts Forbiddance, extending the ward toward the walls. The narrator confirms the ward and its intended exclusion of unwanted extraplanar visitors. Further scenes show him repeating the work and renewing a privacy spell.

Eldin hopes repeated casting will make the protection permanent. The checked scenes show renewal, rather than a completed permanent enchantment. They neither establish a new owner of the castle nor overturn its earlier grant to the company.
